Dedham.wildlife_intro:
Dedham sits between the Charles River, Mother Brook, and wooded reservations, so raccoons, skunks, opossums, and squirrels are never far from a yard. Our most common Dedham jobs are raccoons in chimneys of older Dedham Square and Oakdale homes, gray squirrels in postwar attic spaces, and big brown bats in 19th-century houses in East Dedham, where mill-era construction left plenty of small gaps at eaves and gables.

Riverdale and Greenlodge homeowners also deal with skunks under decks and occasional beaver activity in low, wet areas along the brooks, which we assess within Massachusetts permit rules. In spring we check chimneys and attics for young before sealing, and in fall we focus on the soffit and foundation gaps animals use to get in for winter. Our crew handles wildlife on site under PAC rules and seals the home so the same route is closed for good.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Dedham, MA?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the species, access, and how much sealing and cleanup is involved, so we inspect the home and explain the scope before starting. Older Dedham homes often need chimney and roofline work together, while a simple under-deck skunk job is narrower, and we scope each accordingly.

faqs.q: Why are bats found in East Dedham's older homes?
faqs.a: East Dedham's mill-era and 19th-century houses have layered rooflines, old gable vents, and chimney gaps that suit big brown bats well. Bats are handled by exclusion only, with eviction limited to May 1 through May 31 or August 1 through October 15 under PAC permit conditions, so our crew will inspect and time the work lawfully.

Quincy.wildlife_intro:
Quincy runs from Blue Hills forest to harbor peninsulas, and wildlife follows that whole gradient. In Wollaston, North Quincy, and Quincy Center, Norway rats, raccoons in chimneys, and squirrels in triple-decker attics are the steady calls. In Squantum, Houghs Neck, and Germantown, skunks den under shorefront porches, raccoons raid the marsh edges, and Canada geese gather on waterfront lawns, where they are protected and handled with deterrence only.

The Blue Hills edge brings coyotes into western Quincy conversations and keeps raccoon and opossum pressure high in Merrymount and Montclair. Our crew seals older housing carefully — Quincy's triple-deckers share rooflines and chases, so we check adjoining entry points, not just the obvious one. Spring is raccoon young season in chimneys, and fall is rat and squirrel season indoors. As a MassWildlife-licensed PAC crew, we handle animals on site and close the building up properly.

faqs.q: What does wildlife removal cost in Quincy, MA?
faqs.a: It depends on the animal, the type of building, and how much sealing and cleanup is required, so our crew inspects first and explains the work clearly. Dense Quincy Center housing and a single-family home in Merrymount present different entry-point problems, and the scope follows the building.

faqs.q: I live near the Blue Hills in Quincy and saw a snake — should I be worried?
faqs.a: Most snakes seen in Quincy are harmless species, but the Blue Hills is one of the few Massachusetts areas with state-Endangered copperheads and timber rattlesnakes, which are protected. Do not approach or try to move any snake you cannot identify. Keep distance, keep pets away, and call us or MassWildlife for identification and safety guidance — those protected species are a referral and safety matter, not a removal job.
